title: Working on a color customization system for my 2D Auto-Battler
author: TennDevStudios
selftext:
Hi guys.  I'm working on a 2D auto battler management type fighting game called Battle Tower Manager.  The game itself is still a work in progress, but I wanted to share one feature/system that I've been working on that is coming along pretty well (at least I think).  The game has 70 fighter designs, and each one has every pixel mapped to a region of their sprite/artwork so that I can apply custom color themes, or manually recolor any portion of their clothes/hair/accessories.   It can also apply Shaders in Godot to give hair or clothing effects like flames or lightning or water.

Each fighter was drawn with every outfit piece painted in its own flat "working" color: hair one color, jacket another, shoes another, etc. That gives every pixel a label. A script then reads those colors back into a per-pixel map of which piece each pixel belongs to, while the outline, skin and face stay locked. When you pick a new color, the game shades it across that piece's own light and dark steps, so it still looks hand-shaded. A check recolors every piece by itself on every frame and fails if a single pixel lands in the wrong place.

This sprites, animations, and recoloring system were created entirely with Claude and Codex working in tandem without using any MCP's or tools like asperite. Codex generated the sprites, and the two LLM's together worked out the system to make them consistent and wrote the tools to generate them so that they would re-color cleanly and how to check them. I realize the animation frames leave a little bit to be desired but it's a work in progress.
